feedback.problem:
Complete the following parametric equations generating the hyperbola $\frac{{x}^{2}}{100}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{36}=1$ in terms of the parameter $t,$ defined for $t\in [-\pi ,\pi ]$ where $t\ne \pm \frac{\pi }{2}.$

$x=10\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,$
$y=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a horizontal hyperbola with Cartesian equation

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by

$$
x=a\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=b\operatorname{tan}⁡t.
$$

In our case, $a=\sqrt{100}=10$ and $b=\sqrt{36}=6.$ Therefore, the parametric equations are

$$
x=10\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=6\operatorname{tan}⁡t.
$$
